name: Shimeath
title: David's servant from Benjamin
summary: Shimeath (also known as Shimea or Shimeah) was a Benjamite mentioned in connection with King David's family and servants. The name appears in several contexts in the Old Testament and may refer to different individuals, including a brother of David and a descendant of Benjamin. He is best known as the father of certain servants or warriors during David's time.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Shimeath is mentioned as part of the tribal register of the tribe of Benjamin, as a son of Mikloth in the lineage of Gibeon.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Saul's family
keyEvents.description: Through the tribal register of Benjamin, Shimeath is linked to Saul's royal house, since the lineage of Gibeon includes Saul's ancestors.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in the genealogies of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Shimeath's name is repeated in the parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles chapter 9, confirming his place in the tribe of Benjamin after the return from exile.

keyEvents.title: Shimea as David's brother
keyEvents.description: A person with a similar name, Shimea (Shammah), was David's brother and the father of Jonathan, who killed a giant in battle against the Philistines.
